label: copy-phase input token d (from 2nd fed-back output on)
explanation: Token detector for the fed-back input d during the copy phase. It fires at copy steps where the input is d, meaning the model just output d, and only from recall_idx >= 2 on, where it fires on every such step at a near-constant high value (median ~3.9, max 4.8). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, including when d is an original input. It is weak and only occasional at recall_idx 1, when the fed-back d is orig(0), with values around 0.03-3.5; this is most of the lowest activation quartile. It does not fire on any other input token (fewer than 50 stray activations). Magnitude barely depends on what is output next or on position, as long as recall_idx >= 2.

issues: No systematic counterexamples. On the test split the predicate has 0 false positives (precision 1.0), recall 0.977, F1 0.988, mass recall 0.999 and correlation 0.990.

The misses are 1761 test steps holding only 0.1% of activation mass. All of them are at recall_idx 1 (fed-back d = orig(0)), with tiny values of about 0.01-0.06 relative to the max. This is the weak recall_idx-1 behavior the explanation already describes. Firing at recall_idx 1 is rare: precision there is 0.10, and it covers only about 9% of the lowest activation quartile.
Widening the predicate to recall_idx >= 1 drops F1 to 0.91 (precision 0.84), so the recall_idx >= 2 cutoff is justified.

The profile confirms the other claims. There are 0 activations in the original and delimiter phases. Copy-phase firing is 99.9%+ on in_tok d, with fewer than 50 stray activations on other tokens. Median is 3.91 and max is 4.82. The firing rate is flat at about 0.033 across recall_idx 2-8.
Minor quibble: the explanation says recall_idx-1 activations range up to about 3.5. The sampled misses were much weaker (about 0.05-0.3 absolute), but this does not affect the verdict.
